stories.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj out two weeks with lower-body injury
stories.desc: Xhekaj has missed the team’s last three games, and was in visible pain in practice earlier in the week.

items.title: Canadiens’ Florian Xhekaj out two weeks with lower-body injury
items.desc: Xhekaj has missed the team’s last three games, and was in visible pain in practice earlier in the week.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Canadiens forward Florian Xhekaj is out two weeks with a lower-body injury. He has missed the team's last three games and was in visible pain at practice earlier in the week.

The sample is tiny, so treat this carefully. Xhekaj has played two games so far this season, averaging 7.6 minutes, with no points and 0.08 expected goals, so his results and his chances have lined up. The Canadiens did slightly worse with him on the ice, with their share of expected goals 15.18 points lower when he played, but that comes from about 15 minutes of ice time and says little. The bigger concern is depth, since Montreal sits at 3-3-1 for 7 points. The team controls 55 percent of expected goals at five-on-five, yet goals are running 1.9 below expected and goaltending is 2.6 goals saved below expected. The injury costs them a fourth-line option, not a driver. Montreal's real problem is finishing and saves, which should recover with more games.

stories.title: Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall out week-to-week; Seth Jarvis could return on road trip
stories.desc: The Hurricanes have gone 6-1-1 with Jarvis out of the lineup as he recovers from offseason surgery.

items.title: Hurricanes’ Taylor Hall out week-to-week; Seth Jarvis could return on road trip
items.desc: The Hurricanes have gone 6-1-1 with Jarvis out of the lineup as he recovers from offseason surgery.

stories.take:
Taylor Hall is out week-to-week for the Hurricanes, while Seth Jarvis could return during the upcoming road trip, Daily Faceoff reports. Carolina has gone 6-1-1 without Jarvis as he recovers from offseason surgery.

Hall's absence stings more than his 13.02 minutes a game suggest. So far this season he has 3 goals and 5 points in 8 games, a bit above his 2.22 expected goals, so some of that scoring is a mild overperformance. The underlying play is the real story: Carolina controls 63.48% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him on the ice, and the team's share is 6.98 percentage points better when he plays. The team itself looks strong without being dominant. The Hurricanes own 61.8% of expected goals so far this season, and 58% at 5-on-5. They have scored 1.1 goals fewer than expected, so the results trail the chances. Goaltending has added 0.8 goals above expected. If Jarvis returns as hoped, he helps replace Hall's offense, but Carolina's process has been good enough to absorb a short injury.

stories.desc: David Perron will play for the eighth team in his career.

items.title: David Perron signs with Dallas Stars for his 20th NHL season
items.desc: David Perron will play for the eighth team in his career.

items.title: Stars sign David Perron to one-year contract
items.desc: Perron joins Dallas for his 20th season in the NHL, giving the team some veteran scoring.

stories.take:
Per Daily Faceoff and The Athletic, the Stars have signed David Perron to a one-year contract. The Athletic reports it will be his 20th NHL season and his eighth team, and Daily Faceoff says he gives Dallas some veteran scoring.

Our numbers suggest this team has been better than its 3-3-1 record, but the sample is small, so treat this as seven games so far this season. Dallas has 50.5 percent of the expected goals overall and exactly 50 percent at five-on-five, so the chance quality is dead even. The gap is in finishing. The Stars sit 4.3 goals below expected, which means the shooters have underperformed the quality of their looks, while the goaltending has saved 6.9 goals above expected and is carrying a lot of the load. A veteran scorer could help if the offense stays cold, though one signing does not change the underlying balance. The power play creates 0.69 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows 0.51, so special teams are not the issue. What matters is whether the finishing drifts back toward the chances.

stories.title: Blackhawks' Patrick Kane sets record for assists by U.S.-born player
stories.desc: Patrick Kane tallied his 895th career assist on Connor Bedard's game-opening power-play goal, surpassing the American-born record held by defenseman Phil Housley.

items.title: Blackhawks' Patrick Kane sets record for assists by U.S.-born player
items.desc: Patrick Kane tallied his 895th career assist on Connor Bedard's game-opening power-play goal, surpassing the American-born record held by defenseman Phil Housley.

stories.take:
Per ESPN, Patrick Kane set the record for assists by a U.S.-born player, and later added another on Artyom Levshunov's goal that gave the Blackhawks a 4-3 overtime win, bringing his total to 896.

The milestone is real, but the numbers say Kane is not driving Chicago so far this season. Through seven games he has one goal and two assists, and the Blackhawks control only 36.1 percent of five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice. Chicago is 3.42 percentage points worse with him in the lineup, and his own expected goals (1.26) sit just above his one goal. For fantasy owners, that points to a modest scoring pace rather than a rebound from last year's 57 points in 67 games. Levshunov shows the opposite profile: the team is 8.83 points better with him, yet he has no goals and two assists, 0.91 below his expected total. The bigger problem is team-wide. At 2-5-0, Chicago holds 41.9 percent of expected goals, and its goalies have saved 3.7 goals fewer than expected. Better goaltending would help the record, but the chance quality is lagging too.

stories.title: Brady Tkachuk third in NHL history with back-to-back natural hat tricks
stories.desc: Brady Tkachuk became the second player in almost 40 years and the third player in NHL history to score a natural hat trick -- three consecutive goals without another player from either team scoring -- in back-to-back games.

items.title: Brady Tkachuk third in NHL history with back-to-back natural hat tricks
items.desc: Brady Tkachuk became the second player in almost 40 years and the third player in NHL history to score a natural hat trick -- three consecutive goals without another player from either team scoring -- in back-to-back games.

stories.take:
Brady Tkachuk became the third player in NHL history to score a natural hat trick in back-to-back games, per ESPN, and only the second in almost 40 years to do it. A natural hat trick means three consecutive goals with no one else from either team scoring in between.

The numbers say the finishing is running well ahead of the chances. Tkachuk has 6 goals in 8 games so far this season for FLA, but his own expected goals are 3.38, so he is 2.62 goals above what his shot quality would predict. His 1.42 expected goals per 60 is a solid rate, not a scoring-champion rate, and he is playing just 17.48 minutes a night. For fantasy, that argues for selling into the hot streak rather than projecting this pace. The rest of the picture is steadier: FLA is 4-2-2 with a 53 percent five-on-five share of expected goals, though Tkachuk's team does slightly worse with him on the ice (down 3.42 points of share). His 22 goals in 60 games with OTT last season looks like the better baseline.

stories.title: Leafs’ Tavares leaves game with injury
stories.desc: Tavares collapsed to the ice after Sabres forward Josh Norris slid into his legs early in the third period.

items.title: Leafs’ Tavares leaves game with injury
items.desc: Tavares collapsed to the ice after Sabres forward Josh Norris slid into his legs early in the third period.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Leafs forward John Tavares left the game with an injury after he collapsed to the ice when Sabres forward Josh Norris slid into his legs early in the third period.

The numbers say Toronto can ill afford a long absence. So far this season, TOR sits at 3-3-2 with just 44.5 percent of the expected goals, and 44 percent at five-on-five, meaning the Leafs have been outplayed more often than not. The record has been propped up by luck: they are 3.5 goals above expected, and their goalies have saved 3.6 goals above expected. That kind of cushion rarely lasts, and losing a regular forward makes the underlying problem harder to hide. Buffalo is the mirror image. BUF is 4-3-1 with 52.1 percent of expected goals and 55 percent at five-on-five, yet is 1.4 goals below expected and has a goaltending mark of minus 5.7. Norris has only 1 goal and 1 assist in 8 games, a shade under his 1.24 expected goals, so his slow start looks like noise rather than a decline.

stories.title: Kraken’s Brandon Montour leaves game with lower-body injury
stories.desc: Montour had no goals and five assists in seven games prior to Thursday.

items.title: Kraken’s Brandon Montour leaves game with lower-body injury
items.desc: Montour had no goals and five assists in seven games prior to Thursday.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Kraken defenseman Brandon Montour left Thursday's game with a lower-body injury. He had no goals and five assists in seven games prior to that night.

Montour's results so far this season sit below his underlying work: he has no goals against 1.07 own expected goals, a gap of -1.07, so the scoring drought looks more like finishing luck than a lack of chances. His assists are carrying his points (5 in 8 games), and he averages 22.47 minutes a night, so losing him removes a major piece of Seattle's deployment. The team does better with him on the ice, up 2.54 percentage points in expected goals share, though his 5-on-5 share of 48.13% is middling. Last season he had 11 goals and 32 points in 64 games, which fantasy owners will want to weigh against the unknown injury timeline.

For SEA, the 5-2-1 record (11 points) rests on thin ground. The Kraken own a 47.9% share of expected goals and 47% at 5-on-5, yet they sit at +6.1 goals above expected, with goaltending saving 4.1 goals above expected. Any extended Montour absence tests a team already outscored in chance quality.

stories.title: Toronto Maple Leafs Trade Jacob Quillan, Brandon Buhr To Vancouver Canucks For Aatu Raty
stories.desc: The Toronto Maple Leafs and Vancouver Canucks are shaking up their forward depth.

items.title: Toronto Maple Leafs Trade Jacob Quillan, Brandon Buhr To Vancouver Canucks For Aatu Raty

items.title: Maple Leafs acquire Räty from Canucks for Quillan, Buhr
items.desc: Räty, one of the NHL’s top young faceoff men, cleared waivers earlier on Thursday.

stories.take:
Per The Athletic, the Vancouver Canucks traded Aatu Räty to the Toronto Maple Leafs for two depth forwards, with Daily Faceoff naming them as Jacob Quillan and Brandon Buhr. Daily Faceoff adds that Räty, one of the NHL's top young faceoff men, had cleared waivers earlier on Thursday.

The numbers say Toronto is buying a specialist, not a scorer. Räty has one goal in four games so far this season, and his own expected goals of 0.96 say that goal was about what he'd earned. He averaged just 10.16 minutes a game, and VAN's share of expected goals at 5-on-5 was 28.1% with him on the ice, with the team doing 14.0 points better without him. That is a small sample, but last season's 4 goals and 14 points in 66 games points the same direction. Toronto's own 5-on-5 share of expected goals is 44%, so this is a fourth-line depth move, not a fix. For fantasy, there is little here. The real value is in the faceoff circle, which the site's numbers can't measure.

stories.title: New York Rangers Sign James Reimer To AHL Tryout Amid Goaltending Injuries
stories.desc: With Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo out for the next few weeks, the New York Rangers have turned to veteran goaltender James Reimer for some insurance between the pipes.

items.title: New York Rangers Sign James Reimer To AHL Tryout Amid Goaltending Injuries
items.desc: With Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo out for the next few weeks, the New York Rangers have turned to veteran goaltender James Reimer for some insurance between the pipes.

items.title: Wolf Pack sign James Reimer to professional tryout agreement
items.desc: Reimer posted a 7-4-2 record with a .886 SV% and a 2.42 GAA in 14 appearances for the Ottawa Senators last season.

stories.take:
Per The Hockey News, the Rangers signed goaltender James Reimer to an AHL tryout as insurance, with Igor Shesterkin out for the season and Joonas Korpisalo out for the next few weeks. Daily Faceoff notes Reimer went 7-4-2 with a .886 save percentage and a 2.42 GAA in 14 appearances for Ottawa last season.

The bigger story is what the Rangers are losing in Shesterkin. He has saved 4.88 goals above expected in five games so far this season, a .927 save percentage, after saving 21.47 above expected over 51 games last year. That is the kind of goaltending that props up a team. NYR sit at 6-3-0 with 12 points, and while they own 53.3% of the expected goals, they are scoring 0.9 goals fewer than their chances suggest, so the goalie has been carrying them. The team as a whole is 4.3 goals saved above expected so far this season, and Shesterkin accounts for most of that. A .886 tryout goalie is not a like-for-like replacement, and the 5-on-5 share of 50% leaves little cushion to absorb weaker saves. Expect the Rangers' record to lean much harder on their skaters from here.

stories.title: Ducks’ Mikael Granlund out day-to-day with upper-body injury
stories.desc: The veteran might miss Friday night’s matchup with the Boston Bruins.

items.title: Ducks’ Mikael Granlund out day-to-day with upper-body injury
items.desc: The veteran might miss Friday night’s matchup with the Boston Bruins.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Ducks forward Mikael Granlund is out day-to-day with an upper-body injury, and he might miss Friday night's matchup with the Boston Bruins.

It's a real loss for ANA, because Granlund has been central to how they play so far this season. He has 8 points in 6 games on 2 goals and 6 assists, while logging 19.91 minutes a night. His 5-on-5 share of expected goals is 54.36%, and the team does better with him on the ice by 8.54 percentage points. That matters since ANA as a whole sits at 46% at 5-on-5. He is one of the few things pushing that number up. His 2 goals sit just 0.5 above his 1.5 expected, so the production looks mostly earned. ANA's 4-2-0 record also leans on goaltending, with 2.8 goals saved above expected, and a 48.6% overall expected goals share suggests the team has been slightly outplayed. BOS arrives at 5-2-0 with a 54% 5-on-5 share, a stronger underlying profile, so losing Granlund makes this a tougher night for ANA. For fantasy, treat him as a game-time call until there is an update.

stories.title: Jets’ Josh Morrissey now week-to-week with upper-body injury
stories.desc: Morrissey has been out since Oct. 7 with the injury as the Jets continue their surprisingly hot start to the season.

items.title: Jets’ Josh Morrissey now week-to-week with upper-body injury
items.desc: Morrissey has been out since Oct. 7 with the injury as the Jets continue their surprisingly hot start to the season.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Winnipeg defenseman Josh Morrissey is now week-to-week with an upper-body injury, having been out since Oct. 7 while the Jets continue a surprisingly hot start to the season.

The hot start deserves some skepticism, and Morrissey's absence makes it more pressing. WPG is 4-1-1 with 9 points, but so far this season the Jets hold just 46.8 percent of the expected goals overall and 44 percent at 5-on-5, so they have been outchanced more often than not. Goaltending is carrying them: they have saved 3.0 goals above expected. Morrissey's own sample is tiny, four games and three assists, but the more telling number is that the team's 5-on-5 expected goals share is 6.98 percentage points better with him on the ice. He logged 20.07 minutes a game and posted a 49.57 percent expected goals share himself, so his impact so far this season looks like steady support rather than a driver. Coming off 14 goals and 55 points in 77 games last year, he is a real loss for fantasy owners, and for a Jets team already living on goaltending, a longer absence could expose it.

stories.title: Report: Kings interested in Hellebuyck
stories.desc: The Kings could use the Vezina Trophy winner to help turn things around after a tough start.

items.title: Report: Kings interested in Hellebuyck
items.desc: The Kings could use the Vezina Trophy winner to help turn things around after a tough start.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that the Kings are interested in Connor Hellebuyck, and says the Vezina Trophy winner could help turn things around after a tough start.

The numbers suggest the problem in L.A. is not the skaters. LAK are 0-3-2 with 2 points through 5 games, yet they own 51.4% of the expected goals, a share that stays at 51% at five-on-five. So far this season, they have been slightly better than their opponents at creating quality chances, and the special teams are not the culprit either, with the power play generating 0.71 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.74. The damage shows up in the finishing and in goal: LAK are 2.6 goals below expected, and their goaltending has saved 8.1 goals fewer than expected given the shots faced. That second figure is the one that makes Hellebuyck an obvious fit on paper. It is only five games, so some of this will correct on its own, but a gap that size is exactly where a top goalie changes the math. If the chance quality holds, better goaltending could pull the record back toward what the underlying play says.

stories.title: Canucks’ Filip Chytil to make season debut after shoulder injury
stories.desc: Chytil missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 season after being injured in the preseason.

items.title: Canucks’ Filip Chytil to make season debut after shoulder injury
items.desc: Chytil missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 season after being injured in the preseason.

stories.take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Filip Chytil will make his season debut for the Canucks after missing the first eight games of 2026-27 with a shoulder injury suffered in the preseason.

The timing matters, because Vancouver (2-6-1, 5 points) has been outplayed so far this season. VAN holds just 41.0% of the expected goals, and its 5-on-5 share is also 41%, so the underlying play matches the record. Chytil's return won't fix that alone, but it's worth noting that a Vancouver line-up without him has produced real trouble creating chances. Goaltending hasn't helped either: the team sits at -7.8 goals saved above expected, though VAN is plus 5.0 in goals minus expected, so finishing has been propping up the results more than the process has earned.

The Chytil numbers are one game, so treat them lightly. He played 18.5 minutes, set up one goal and had 0.05 expected goals. His 5-on-5 expected goals share was only 8.36%, and VAN's share was 32.64 percentage points better with him off the ice. That's a rusty first night, not a verdict. Last season he scored 3 goals in 12 games, so the real question is how quickly he finds his legs.

stories.title: Blackhawks’ Bowen Byram day-to-day with upper-body injury
stories.desc: Byram was hit by a shot during Chicago’s game on Tuesday against the Penguins.

items.title: Blackhawks’ Bowen Byram day-to-day with upper-body injury
items.desc: Byram was hit by a shot during Chicago’s game on Tuesday against the Penguins.

stories.take:
Per Daily Faceoff, Blackhawks defenseman Bowen Byram is day-to-day with an upper-body injury after being hit by a shot during Chicago's Tuesday game against the Penguins.

Chicago can ill afford to lose a top-pairing minute-eater. Byram has logged 24.7 minutes a game so far this season, and the team around him is struggling: the Blackhawks are 2-5-0 and own just 41.9 percent of the expected goals overall, 38 percent at five-on-five. Byram's own five-on-five share sits at 38.36 percent, so he's not dragging the team down so much as swimming with the current. The team is basically as good with him as without him (-0.06 percentage points). Offensively, he has one assist in six games against 0.4 expected goals of his own, so he is slightly under his chances, though the sample is tiny. Last season in Buffalo he scored 11 goals and 42 points in 82 games. For fantasy owners, a short absence is a minor hit, but a long one would shift heavy minutes to a thinner blue line on a team already giving up too much.

stories.title: Avalanche Assistant Dave Hakstol Hired As Head Coach Of Arizona State University
stories.desc: After spending the last 10 seasons in the NHL as a coach, Dave Hakstol is returning to his roots at the NCAA level.

items.title: Avalanche Assistant Dave Hakstol Hired As Head Coach Of Arizona State University
items.desc: After spending the last 10 seasons in the NHL as a coach, Dave Hakstol is returning to his roots at the NCAA level.

stories.take:
The Hockey News reports that Avalanche assistant Dave Hakstol has been hired as head coach of Arizona State University, returning to the NCAA after 10 seasons coaching in the NHL. Daily Faceoff adds that Colorado has hired Brett McLean as an assistant to replace him.

The timing lands on a team that has little obviously broken so far this season. Colorado is 4-2-1 with 9 points through 7 games and controls 57.3% of the expected goals, with 56% at 5-on-5, so the process is strong. The power play generates 0.76 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allows just 0.34 per game, which suggests the special teams structure is working. The wrinkle is in the finishing and saving: COL has scored 7.8 goals more than expected, while its goaltending is at -3.7 goals saved above expected. The offense is running hot and the goaltending cold. That is a small sample, so neither should be read as permanent, and the new assistant's job is mostly to keep a sound underlying game intact while those results settle.

stories.title: Ducks' Tristan Luneau is ready to live up to expectations after surprising extension
stories.desc: The Ducks signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year, $43.2 million contract extension despite his having played only 14 career NHL games.

items.title: Ducks' Tristan Luneau is ready to live up to expectations after surprising extension
items.desc: The Ducks signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year, $43.2 million contract extension despite his having played only 14 career NHL games.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that the Ducks signed defenseman Tristan Luneau to a six-year, $43.2 million contract extension despite his having played only 14 career NHL games.

The early numbers are decent but not yet a justification. So far this season, Luneau has played 21.89 minutes a game across six games, with no goals and one assist. His own expected goals are 0.31, so he is 0.31 below that mark, which is a tiny gap on a tiny sample. At 5-on-5, the Ducks hold 50.4 percent of the expected goals with him on the ice, and the team is 5.5 percentage points better with him out there than without him. That is a real positive on a club that sits at 46 percent at 5-on-5 and 48.6 percent overall, though Anaheim's 4-2-0 record leans on goals saved above expected (+2.8) and scoring 1.3 above expected, not on controlling play. The big minutes show the coaching staff already trusts him, but six games cannot confirm the contract. The deal is a bet on what he becomes, and his early on-ice impact is the first modest evidence for it.

items.title: NHL contract grades: Red Wings lock down Alex DeBrincat at fair rate for top scorer

items.title: Projecting Simon Edvinsson's Next Potential Contract With The Detroit Red Wings
items.desc: Detroit Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff says he has no interest in trading defenseman Simon Edvinsson, but time is running out. How will this showdown end?

stories.take:
Per The Athletic, the Red Wings and Alex DeBrincat have agreed to a seven-year extension carrying a $13 million average annual value, which keeps him in Detroit through 2034, when he will be 36. The Athletic's contract grades piece calls it a fair rate for a top scorer.

The early numbers back the idea that he's still the engine. Through six games so far this season, DeBrincat has four goals and eight points while averaging 20.17 minutes, and he has scored 0.89 more goals than his chances predicted (3.11 expected goals). At five-on-five he owns 60.17% of the expected goals while on the ice, and Detroit's share of the play is 14.21 percentage points better with him out there. The model projects 1.36 expected goals per 60 for him, which fits a player coming off 41 goals and 85 points in 82 games last season. The risk is the back end of the deal, but the production gives no sign of slipping yet. The team around him is the bigger concern. Detroit sits at 1-3-2 with a 49.9% share of expected goals and has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances suggest, so the results have lagged the play. A scorer this steady is the kind of player who can help close that gap.

stories.title: Hurricanes' Jordan Staal to miss 1 to 2 months with torn calf
stories.desc: Jordan Staal, the reigning Conn Smythe Trophy winner, is the heart and soul of the Hurricanes.

items.title: Hurricanes' Jordan Staal to miss 1 to 2 months with torn calf
items.desc: Jordan Staal, the reigning Conn Smythe Trophy winner, is the heart and soul of the Hurricanes.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Jordan Staal will miss one to two months with a torn calf, and it describes the reigning Conn Smythe Trophy winner as the heart and soul of the Hurricanes.

The numbers suggest the loss is real but not a disaster. Staal has no goals or points in six games so far this season, though his own expected goals of 0.95 mean he was due something, a gap of -0.95 that bad luck explains better than his play. His 45.37 percent share of 5-on-5 expected goals is below even, and CAR's share of expected goals is 14.82 points worse with him on the ice, so it is hard to argue he was driving play this fall. He played 15.56 minutes a night, and last season he scored 20 goals and 36 points in 75 games. Carolina is 6-1-1 and controls 61.8 percent of expected goals overall (58 percent at 5-on-5), so the team's foundation does not rest on him. The cost will show in depth and in the 0.47 expected goals per game the penalty kill allows, where veteran forwards matter. Fantasy owners should not expect his production to rebound quickly.

stories.title: Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard expected to make season debut against Sidney Crosby, Penguins
stories.desc: Connor Bedard was initially expected to be out until early November, but his rehab has gone better than expected.

items.title: Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard expected to make season debut against Sidney Crosby, Penguins
items.desc: Connor Bedard was initially expected to be out until early November, but his rehab has gone better than expected.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Connor Bedard is expected to make his season debut against Sidney Crosby and the Penguins, after a rehab that went better than expected. He had initially been expected to be out until early November.

Chicago could use him. The Blackhawks are 2-5-0 and have controlled just 41.9 percent of expected goals so far this season, falling to 38 percent at 5-on-5, with goalies that have cost them 3.7 goals compared to an average result. Bedard's one game so far this season is a thin sample, but the signs are good: he played 21.1 minutes, generated 0.41 expected goals and held a 60.09 percent 5-on-5 expected goals share. The model puts his rate at 1.14 expected goals per 60, and the team's results run 22.86 percentage points better with him on the ice. That is a big swing for a club this far underwater, and a reminder that his 30 goals and 75 points in 69 games last season came from real chance creation. Pittsburgh, at 3-3-1 and 50.9 percent of expected goals, has been steadier, though Crosby's 47.82 percent 5-on-5 share suggests he has not driven play this year.

stories.title: Nico Sturm's head injury rattles Wild with Faber flashbacks: 'All I thought of was Brock'
stories.desc: Nico Sturm left the game during the first period after taking an errant shot to the head.

items.title: Nico Sturm's head injury rattles Wild with Faber flashbacks: 'All I thought of was Brock'
items.desc: Nico Sturm left the game during the first period after taking an errant shot to the head.

stories.take:
The Athletic reports that Nico Sturm left the Wild's game during the first period after taking an errant shot to the head. The outlet's headline notes the incident brought back memories of Brock Faber, but gives no word yet on the severity of the injury or how long he might be out.

Sturm's loss is unlikely to shift the Wild's fortunes much. He has played only 9.04 minutes a night over 3 games so far this season, with no points and 0.04 expected goals, so the sample is tiny. Still, his 5-on-5 expected goals share of 42.53% and the team's 7.62 percentage point dip in expected goals share with him on the ice suggest the Wild have been slightly better without him. Last season he managed 5 goals and 11 points in 49 games, which fits a bottom-six role. MIN sits at 4-2-1 with 9 points, but the 48% 5-on-5 expected goals share and a goals-minus-expected of -2.1 show the record leans on goaltending, with 4.7 goals saved above expected. Whoever replaces Sturm will not hurt that picture much, but the Wild need their 5-on-5 play to improve.
